description: Lesson i8 mistake: hal-spi-595 with SPI_FIRSTBIT_LSB - the 74HC595 chaser runs backwards (QH ... QA)
expect:
72 MHz. SPI1 master mode 0, LSB FIRST (the only difference from hal-spi-595), 8-bit, SCK 72 MHz / 16 = 4.5 MHz on PA5, MOSI PA7 (AF push-pull); PA4 = 74HC595 RCLK (push-pull, low after init). 74HC595: SER = PA7, SRCLK = PA5, RCLK = PA4, SRCLR high, OE low, QA..QH -> LED + resistor to GND. USART1 PA9/PA10 115200 8N1 sends '74HC595 chaser 10 Hz
' once. Then on the next HAL tick and every 100 ms after it (deadline based, no drift): RCLK low, one byte 1 << step clocked out (8 SCK pulses, 111 ns half period), RCLK high (rising edge = latch), step = 0..7 cyclically: because the bit sent first ends in QH, QH, QG, ... QA light one at a time for 100 ms each (800 ms cycle) - the chaser runs backwards. PA4 is high except for a pulse of about 5 us around each transfer.

circuit: PA5, PA7, PA4: 74HC595 (SRCLK, SER, RCLK; SRCLR to 3V3, OE to GND), QA-QH: LED + 220 ohm to GND
USART1: virtual terminal on PA9 (TX) / PA10 (RX)
